scenes.heading: Troubleshooting
scenes.narration: Env Setup. Troubleshooting. In this video we review 8 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What is the first troubleshooting step when something is not working in a local AEM environment?
scenes.heading: Check Package Manager to verify the package was actually installed
scenes.body: The first troubleshooting step is to check Package Manager (`http://localhost:4502/crx/packmgr`) to confirm the package was actually installed. Many issues arise from packages that failed to install silently.

scenes.heading: http://localhost:4502/crx/packmgr

scenes.question: What AEM tool do you use to verify that a node exists in the JCR and has the correct content?
scenes.heading: CRXDE Lite
scenes.body: CRXDE Lite (accessed at `http://localhost:4502/crx/de`) is the browser-based JCR explorer. It lets you browse the full repository node tree, check node properties, and verify that deployed content landed in the correct paths.

scenes.question: What AEM console do you use to check whether an OSGi bundle is in Active state?
scenes.heading: The Bundle Console at /system/console/bundles
scenes.body: The OSGi Bundle Console at `http://localhost:4502/system/console/bundles` shows all installed OSGi bundles and their states. An `Active` state means the bundle is running correctly. `Installed` or `Resolved` states usually indicate a missing dependency.

scenes.question: Where is the AEM error.log file located?
scenes.heading: crx-quickstart/logs/error.log
scenes.body: The `error.log` file is located at `crx-quickstart/logs/error.log` — inside the `crx-quickstart` folder created by the QuickStart Jar. AEM logs all errors, warnings, and info messages here. It is the primary log for troubleshooting.

scenes.question: Which AEM URL provides clientlib debug tools for front-end troubleshooting?
scenes.heading: /libs/granite/ui/content/dumplibs.html
scenes.body: The clientlib debug page is at `/libs/granite/ui/content/dumplibs.html`. It shows all registered client libraries, their categories, dependencies, and included files — useful for debugging missing CSS, JavaScript, or incorrect clientlib loading order.

scenes.question: What are the two most common errors when setting up a local AEM environment?
scenes.heading: Wrong Java version and trying to double-click the QuickStart Jar
scenes.body: The two most common errors are: (1) using the wrong Java version — AEM requires JDK 21, and (2) double-clicking the QuickStart Jar instead of starting it with `java -jar` from the command line. Both cause the AEM instance to fail to start correctly.
